:::{#rem-prediction-bias-integral .remark}
#### The bias as an iterated expectation and as integrals

The [new observation](#def-new-observation) is [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) of the [training set](#def-training-set).
So by the [law of iterated expectations](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-lie),
the expectation in @eq-prediction-bias can be taken in two steps:
first over the new outcome with the training set fixed,
then over the [training sets](#def-training-set).

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \Expfc{\trainset}{\Expfc{\newoutvar}{\prederr_{*}\paren{\fitmodf{\trainset}} \mid \trainset, \newpredvar = \predvar}}.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias-iterated}

The training set consists of $\nobs$ [independent and identically distributed](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-iid) pairs $\paren{\Predvar_\iobs, \Outvar_\iobs}$,
so its density is the product of the densities of its pairs.
When the variables are [continuous](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-continuous-rv), the two steps are integrals.
The inner integral runs over the new outcome $\outvar$,
and the outer integral runs over the values $\paren{\predvar_\iobs, \outvar_\iobs}$ of the training pairs,
which determine the [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) $\predvalf{\predvar}$:

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \int \cdots \int
\paren{\int \paren{\predvalf{\predvar} - \outvar} \p(\newoutvar = \outvar \mid \newpredvar = \predvar) \, d\outvar}
\prod_{\iobs = 1}^{\nobs} \p(\Predvar_\iobs = \predvar_\iobs,\, \Outvar_\iobs = \outvar_\iobs)
\, d\predvar_1 \, d\outvar_1 \cdots d\predvar_\nobs \, d\outvar_\nobs.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias-integral}

For [discrete variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv), the integrals are sums.

:::
